methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Virginia Beach schools bring ChatGPT under division oversight as AI use grows - 13newsnow.com
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Beach schools bringing ChatGPT under division oversight signals shallow, platform-mediated AI adoption spreading beyond NoVA metro hubs—distribution without deep capability development, as students consume rather than build AI tools.

signals.title: AI pressure grows on Richmond's young workforce - Axios
signals.signal_reading: AI pressure on Richmond's young workforce indicates concentration of transformation demands in metro areas with existing tech infrastructure, likely deepening the capability gap as rural regions face different economic pressures without comparable AI integration imperatives.

signals.title: Norfolk could get AI assist for non-emergency calls - Yahoo
signals.signal_reading: Norfolk deploying AI for non-emergency dispatch represents shallow, vendor-delivered AI adoption in a mid-tier metro—distributed geographically but not building local AI development capacity, reinforcing platform dependency rather than indigenous expertise.

signals.title: Parents call for less screen time, more intentional use of technology in schools
signals.signal_reading: Parent resistance to school technology in rural Southwest/Southside regions signals potential barriers to AI fluency development in already-underserved areas, risking deeper exclusion from AI-enabled economic opportunities as metro areas accelerate adoption.

signals.title: McLean data center power-focused startup to be acquired for $232.28M
signals.signal_reading: A $232M acquisition of a McLean data center infrastructure startup exemplifies deep technical capability and capital concentration in NoVA, reinforcing the region's dominance in AI-enabling infrastructure while other Virginia regions remain consumer markets rather than innovation centers.
